question.:question/problem: Which of the following diagrams gives the slope field at the points indicated for the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=(-1)x^{2}-(1)y^{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We have to sketch the slope field at the points $(-1,-1)$,$(1,1)$,$(1,0)$.

To sketch the slope field at the given points, we substitute their coordinates into the right-hand side of the differential equation.

$$
\begin{aligned} & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(-1,-1)}=(-1)(-1)^{2}-1(-1)^{2}=-2, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(1,1)}=(-1)(1)^{2}-1(1)^{2}=-2, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(1,0)}=(-1)(1)^{2}-1(0)^{2}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting up our points and drawing our line segments, we get the following diagram.
